title: Cluster-level summary analysis for few clusters
summary: The difference in mean cluster proportion between arms of a cluster trial, from a t-test on the cluster summaries with (clusters - 2) degrees of freedom.

sizing._note: A cluster trial is sized by simulation or a design-effect calculation on the number of clusters; the individual two-proportions form is wrong.

pinned_defaults: Both: one value per CLUSTER; the cluster is the unit of analysis.
Both: the classical pooled-variance t on (clusters - 2) df (var.equal = TRUE / equal_var=True), intervention first.
_when: Under about 30 clusters, individual-level sandwich and GEE standard errors are too small. Cluster-level summaries are simple and valid; they estimate the difference in the AVERAGE CLUSTER proportion, equal to the patient-level difference when clusters are equal in size. With unequal sizes, weight by size or use a small-sample-corrected model.
